speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To begin my assessment, have these symptoms been present for more than a few weeks, and have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits or appetite?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the duration and weight loss are significant. Have you experienced any fever, cough, or changes in bowel habits like diarrhea or constipation? Also, have you noticed any lumps in your neck or groin?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the update; the description of a painless, fixed supraclavicular node is highly concerning. Given the systemic symptoms of fever, night sweats, and significant weight loss, can you describe the nature of your abdominal pain and any associated changes in bowel habits? Please also tell me if you have a known history of Crohn's disease or tuberculosis, and if you have noticed any skin ulcers or oral sores.

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP, LDH, and TST/IGRA.
REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_XRay, Abdominal_US.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The test results showing normal readings for CBC, ESR, CRP, LDH, and TST/IGRA are surprising given your significant "B" symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss) and fixed supraclavicular lymphadenopathy. Can you confirm if the abdominal pain is specifically in the right upper or lower quadrant, and have you experienced any bone pain, skin lesions, or a feeling of fullness after small meals?

REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_CT.

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The sensation of fullness after small meals and tighter clothing strongly suggests hepatomegaly or splenomegaly. Can you confirm if you have noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), and have you had any recent fevers or unexplained bruising?

REQUEST TEST: Liver Function Panel (AST, ALT, ALP, Bilirubin), PT/INR.
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_CT.
